stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: A distant star sends parallel rays into the telescope. The objective lens converges them to an intermediate image at its focal plane; the eyepiece then relays that image to your eye. Sweep the three sliders — objective focal length $f'_1$, eyepiece focal length $f'_2$, and lens spacing $d$ — and watch the ray bundle reshape.
stages.concept: In the afocal setup, $d = f'_1 + f'_2$: the back focal plane of the objective coincides with the front focal plane of the eyepiece ($F'_1 \equiv F_2$). Parallel rays in $\rightarrow$ parallel rays out, magnified in angle: $G = f'_1 / f'_2 = \alpha' / \alpha$.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: Match each of the 3 target magnifications in sequence. Adjust $f'_1$ and $f'_2$ so their ratio equals $G^*$, then set $d = f'_1 + f'_2$ so the exit rays are parallel (afocal). Both indicators must be green — then press Confirm.
stages.concept: Two constraints, three sliders: pick any $f'_2$, then $f'_1 = G^* \cdot f'_2$, and $d = f'_1 + f'_2$. Long objective + short eyepiece $\Rightarrow$ big magnification.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: The rays are hidden. For each target $G^*$: compute $f'_1$, $f'_2$, $d$ on paper so that $f'_1 / f'_2 = G^*$ and $d = f'_1 + f'_2$, set the sliders, then Fire. One shot per target — miss any and the setup resets.
stages.concept: Afocal: $d = f'_1 + f'_2$. Magnification: $G = f'_1 / f'_2 = \alpha' / \alpha$. Both conditions must hold — the ratio decides $G$, the sum decides parallel exit.

labels.peek_line1: Afocal: d = f'₁ + f'₂  ·  Ratio: G = f'₁ / f'₂
labels.peek_line2: Pick f'₂ freely, then f'₁ = G* × f'₂ and d = f'₁ + f'₂
labels.tip1: sweep all three sliders — ratio sets G, sum sets afocal
labels.tip2: match G* AND afocal — both green, then CONFIRM
labels.tip3: compute f'₁, f'₂, d on paper — one shot per target

1.1: Try doubling f'₁ — the intermediate image slides right, and G doubles.
1.2: Try halving f'₂ — G doubles again. Small eyepiece = big magnification.
1.3: For clean parallel exit, set d = f'₁ + f'₂ exactly. Any other spacing and the rays fan out or converge.

2.1: Read G* from the target line. Aim for f'₁/f'₂ ≈ G*.
2.2: Pick f'₂ first (any value in range), then set f'₁ = G* × f'₂.
2.3: Once G is green, tune d until it equals f'₁ + f'₂ — the afocal bar turns green. Then Confirm.

3.1: You have exactly one shot per target. Compute f'₁, f'₂, d on paper first.
3.2: Two equations: f'₁ = G* × f'₂ (any f'₂ in [8, 40] works), then d = f'₁ + f'₂.
3.3: Peek shows the strategy — it doesn't reveal the answer. Set sliders, then Fire.
